channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: STF determina que TRE-RR reveja regra de descompatibilização para eleição suplementar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered the Regional Electoral Court of Roraima (TRE-RR) to reconsider the calendar for the supplementary gubernatorial election, currently set for June 21, due to concerns over the incompatibility rule. The decision aims to ensure the election complies with electoral law, preventing undue advantages for candidates still holding public office. The measure is part of efforts to uphold the integrity and equal conditions in the supplementary electoral process.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei para criar a 1ª Universidade Federal Indígena do Brasil
item.description: President Lula signed into law the creation of Brazil's first Federal Indigenous University (Unind), headquartered in Brasília with campuses across the country. Developed with input from the Ministries of Education and Indigenous Peoples, FUNAI, and the National Forum for Indigenous School Education, the university aims to serve Indigenous communities through programs in territorial management, Indigenous languages, health, agroecology, and more. The rector and vice-rector must be Indigenous, and operations are set to begin in 2027.

item.title: Presidente do PT diz que sigla terá “palanque forte” em Minas
item.description: National PT president Edinho Silva stated the party is working to consolidate state-level electoral slates for Lula's 2026 re-election campaign, noting São Paulo is 'resolved' and Minas Gerais is being reorganized after Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) declined to run for governor. Although the Senate slate in São Paulo is still under construction, the PT affirmed it has leadership to build strong slates and announced Edinho will travel to Belo Horizonte for meetings with leaders, militants, and potential pre-candidates.

item.title: Lula sanciona criação de Universidade Federal Indígena
item.description: President Lula sanctioned the creation of Brazil’s first Federal Indigenous University, headquartered in Brasília, offering 10 undergraduate programs, 2,800 student slots, and education rooted in traditional knowledge. The institution, developed through over 20 seminars with Indigenous communities since 2024, provides training in teacher education, Indigenous health, and territorial and environmental management. Lula emphasized that the university restores to Indigenous peoples the right to knowledge that was unjustly taken from them.

item.title: Esquerda derrota direita nas redes sociais no embate sobre o fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The left dominated the social media debate on ending the 6×1 work scale, with 55% of publications and 41% of interactions, compared to 26% and 28% for the right, according to Instituto Democracia em Xeque. The bill, approved in the Chamber with a phased transition to a 40-hour workweek within a year, was driven by figures like Erika Hilton and Rick Azevedo, while the right accused the Lula government of electoral tactics. The proposal now moves to the Federal Senate.

item.title: O apelo de Douglas Ruas a Fachin para assumir imediatamente o governo do Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), president of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly, appealed to Supreme Court Justice Edson Fachin to immediately appoint him as governor, claiming his election as assembly president places him first in the line of succession. The governorship has been vacant since Cláudio Castro’s resignation in March, with interim governance led by Ricardo Couto, president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice. Ruas argues that Couto’s continued role is no longer justified and that his administrative acts may be constitutionally flawed.

item.title: Brasil e Suriname vão negociar acordo para ampliar comércio
item.description: Brazil and Suriname have launched negotiations to expand their bilateral trade agreement, with talks set to begin in the second half of 2026. The meeting between President Lula and Surinamese President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons resulted in the approval of terms of reference to increase trade flows, currently at just $55 million in 2025, and to include new sectors such as energy, logistics, agribusiness, and critical minerals.

item.title: Douglas Ruas aciona STF para assumir governo do Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas, president of the Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro, petitioned Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux to immediately install him as governor of the state, arguing that his election to the legislative presidency places him in the line of succession. The request was filed as a direct action before the STF, seeking his investiture and effective exercise of the governor's office.

item.title: Escala 6x1: oposição irá mesmo sustentar a PEC ‘pró-liberdade’ no Senado?
item.description: Columnist Fernando Schüler criticizes the Chamber of Deputies' vote on ending the 6x1 work scale as a 'demagoguery show', noting the opposition shifted from opposing reduced hours to advocating a more radical 3-day weekly leave. He expects the Senate to foster a more logical debate, particularly through Senator Rogério Marinho’s proposal for individual work contract flexibility as an alternative to CLT, allowing negotiated 15h, 20h, or 30h weekly schedules with proportional benefits.

item.title: O espelho da desordem: a guerra de Trump e o caos brasileiro
item.description: Trump's return to the White House signifies a programmatic 'war' against the establishment, with clear goals such as reducing the state and economic protectionism. In contrast, Brazil's political chaos is an end in itself, driven by short-termism, budgetary maneuvers, public and legal insecurity, and the absence of a long-term plan, which deters investment and perpetuates the status quo. The lack of a twenty-year plan and institutional decay stand in stark contrast to Washington's deliberate strategy.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede vista e suspende julgamento sobre flexibilização da Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes requested a view and suspended the judgment on the flexibility of the Clean Record Law, delaying analysis for up to 90 days. The rapporteur, Justice Cármen Lúcia, had already opposed the changes, arguing they represent a social and ethical setback that weakens electoral morality, a stance followed by Justice Luiz Fux. The proposal would shift the start of the eight-year ineligibility period from the end of the sentence to the date of conviction and cap total ineligibility at 12 years, potentially benefiting politicians such as Anthony Garotinho, José Roberto Arruda, and Eduardo Cunha.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede vista e suspende julgamento que discute mudança na Lei da Ficha Limpa que reduz prazo de inelegibilidade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes requested a view and suspended the judgment on the constitutionality of the 2025 amendments to the Clean Record Law, which reduced the ineligibility period for convicted politicians. So far, Justices Luiz Fux and Cármen Lúcia have voted to declare the changes unconstitutional, arguing they undermine the law and represent a setback in the fight against impunity. The trial is taking place in the Court's virtual plenary and was scheduled to end this Friday (29).

item.title: Presidente do PT define votação da 6 X 1 como “surpreendente”
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva called the Chamber's approval of the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule 'surprising,' with 461 votes in favor and 19 against in the second round, and expressed confidence that the Senate will prioritize the proposal to reduce the workweek to 40 hours. He described it as a 'correction of a historical injustice' against workers, crediting President Lula's efforts and broad congressional sensitization, despite strained relations with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following the rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Gilmar suspende julgamento sobre Lei da Ficha Limpa; placar é de 2x0 para vetar flexibilização
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes suspended the judgment on amendments to the Clean Record Law made by Congress by issuing a request for view (more time for analysis). The partial score was 2x0 in favor of maintaining the law's strictness and rejecting any flexibility. The decision postpones the definition of whether politicians convicted in second instance can run for office again.

item.title: Presidente do PT minimiza encontro de Flávio Bolsonaro com Trump
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva downplayed Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's meeting with Donald Trump, calling it 'political marketing'. He defended Lula's U.S. visit as institutional, focused on Brazilian interests such as rare earths sovereignty, energy transition, and global peace, stating Lula is now the most respected democratic leader internationally.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que cria primeira Universidade Federal Indígena do país
item.description: President Lula signed into law the creation of the Federal Indigenous University (Unind), the first higher education institution in Brazil dedicated exclusively to Indigenous peoples, headquartered in Brasília with campuses across the country. Set to begin operations in 2027, Unind will initially offer 10 courses focused on territorial management, Indigenous languages, health, agroecology, and teacher training, serving 2,800 students with 366 faculty members. The law mandates that the rector and vice-rector must be Indigenous faculty, as approved by Congress.

item.title: Bolsonaro vai bater martelo sobre nome do PL para substituir Cláudio Castro na disputa ao Senado
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro will decide between today and tomorrow who will replace Cláudio Castro as the PL’s Senate candidate, after the former Rio de Janeiro governor withdrew from the race due to Federal Police investigations into alleged favors to Refit and investments by Rioprevidência. The decision will follow a meeting with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, considering a shortlist of Sóstenes Cavalcante, Carlos Portinho, and Carlos Jordy. Castro stated he must focus entirely on his legal defense and family.

item.title: Cláudio Castro desiste de disputar Senado após ser alvo da PF por relação com Vorcaro
item.description: Cláudio Castro withdrew his Senate pre-candidacy for Rio de Janeiro after being targeted by the Federal Police over alleged ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro. He informed PL president Valdemar Costa Neto and released a statement citing personal and familial reflection amid public exposure and accusations. Although already ineligible due to a TSE conviction, the Vorcaro investigation effectively ended his political comeback, with the PL now considering alternatives such as Sóstenes Cavalcante and Carlos Jordy.

item.title: Caiado diz que PT “atrasou o Brasil” e exalta avanço do agro
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) accused the PT of having 'set Brazil back by 20 years' in a social media video, while praising the advancement of Brazilian agribusiness, attributing it to the sector's 'competence' and investments made. The rhetoric reinforces his critical stance toward the current government and his defense of agribusiness as a national development engine.

item.title: Câmara aprova PEC que estende imunidade tributária de entidades religiosas; acompanhe
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first round PEC 5/23, extending tax immunity of religious entities to include taxes on the purchase of goods and services necessary for their operations. The proposal, reported by Deputy Dr. Fernando Máximo (União-RO), aims to correct a perceived distortion that burdens charitable entities with embedded taxes, arguing this encourages job creation abroad over domestic economic growth. The measure depends on a complementary law to define national eligibility criteria and will be voted on in a second round shortly.

item.title: Caso Master: PF analisará nova proposta de delação de Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: The Federal Police informed the STF that it will analyze a potential new plea bargain proposal from Daniel Vorcaro, former CEO of Banco Master, if submitted to the PGR. Last week, the PF and PGR rejected the defense's annexes as insufficient. There is no deadline for Vorcaro to submit a new version, and investigations continue regardless of the agreement.

item.title: Cláudio Castro se pronuncia após retirar candidatura ao Senado
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) announced the withdrawal of his pre-candidacy for the Federal Senate following two Federal Police operations linked to the Banco Master case and alleged favors to Refit. He described the decision as the 'most difficult of his life' due to narratives and half-truths affecting his family, while also noting his ineligibility ruled by the TSE in March for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. Castro stated he will now focus on his defense and clearing the accusations, expressing confidence in the institutions.

item.title: PSB decide lançar Márcio França ao Senado por São Paulo
item.description: The PSB has decided to launch Márcio França as its pre-candidate for the Senate in São Paulo, although the decision still depends on a conversation between Lula and the party’s national president, João Campos. The move comes amid a deadlock in the Haddad-led (PT) ticket, where Simone Tebet (PSB) is seen as the consolidated name for one seat, while the second seat is contested between França and Marina Silva (Rede), with internal PSB resistance to Marina’s candidacy due to her 30% rejection rate in recent polls.

item.title: Com desistência de Castro, aliados de Flávio veem Sóstenes com mais apoio para disputar Senado e Jordy correndo por fora
item.description: The withdrawal of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro from the Senate race prompted the PL to accelerate the reorganization of its bolsonarist slate in the state, with federal deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante gaining strength as the leading candidate to run alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Flávio is expected to make the final decision by next week, while deputy Carlos Jordy, despite ideological support, remains a secondary option due to his limited grassroots reach. The move reflects the party's effort to prevent Castro's legal troubles from undermining Bolsonaro's national presidential pre-campaign strategy.

item.title: A avaliação de Gilmar sobre o impeachment, no documentário sobre Temer
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes stated that impeachment in Brazil functions as a 'parliamentarization of presidentialism', used as a political solution when presidents fail to build congressional majorities. The comment was made in the documentary '963 Dias' about the Temer government, and echoed by former Chamber President Rodrigo Maia, who criticized the individualistic nature of how the Chamber president decides on impeachment requests.

item.title: Lula: “Meninada” quer trabalhar 36 horas e “ser feliz” fora do trabalho
item.description: President Lula praised the progress in reducing Brazil's workweek from 44 to 36 hours, stating that younger generations want to work less to have time to be happy outside work. He noted the PEC was approved in two rounds of voting in Congress with strong majorities and that the government aims to implement the change with a 60-day transition to take effect before the October elections. Lula linked the reform to modernizing labor relations and his re-election campaign, while also mentioning cooperation with Suriname.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro oferece cargo para Alvaro Dias abrir mão da candidatura ao Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is offering Alvaro Dias the role of Southern region campaign coordinator and a potential ministerial position in exchange for withdrawing from the Senate race. The effort, led by his campaign team, aims to consolidate presidential support in southern Brazil. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Projeto com maior proteção para 600 mil brasileiros com diabetes 1 vai virar lei
item.description: Brazil's Congress has approved Bill PL 5.868/2025, which strengthens protections for approximately 600,000 Brazilians living with type 1 diabetes, ensuring access to free medication, medical devices, workplace and school accommodations, and protection against discrimination. Authored by Senator Randolfe Rodrigues (PT-AP) and reported by Senator Humberto Costa (PT-PE), the bill now awaits presidential sanction.

item.title: Lula firma pacto militar com Suriname para fronteiras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) signed 13 agreements with Suriname’s President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons (NDP), focusing on security, defense, and transnational crime, including a memorandum for coordinated military operations along the Amazon border. The agreements cover cybersecurity, human trafficking prevention, public health, science and technology, disaster management, and maritime integration, strengthening bilateral cooperation in the region. Lula emphasized multilateralism and regional integration as pathways to peace, stating both nations believe in cooperation that respects national sovereignty.

item.title: Na mira da indústria por 6x1, Lula avalia se irá a debate da CNI
item.description: President Lula has not yet confirmed his attendance at the CNI debate scheduled for June 22, following criticism from the industrial sector over his agreement with Congress to end the 6x1 work schedule. CNI President Ricardo Alban called the deal 'strictly electoral' and said the 60-day adaptation timeline undermines business planning, especially for small and medium enterprises. Confirmed attendees include pre-candidates Ronaldo Caiado (União Brasil) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ).

item.title: Chanchada de Flávio com Trump pode acabar em duplo naufrágio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro staged a diversionary appearance with Donald Trump in the U.S. to shift focus from his alleged ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro, central to the Banco Master scandal. The move is seen as a media-savvy tactic to overshadow ongoing investigations.

item.title: PSB cogita lançar Tebet e Márcio França ao Senado em São Paulo à revelia do PT
item.description: The PSB is considering nominating Simone Tebet and Márcio França for the São Paulo Senate seat without PT's approval, due to the party's indecision on the state electoral slate. The decision hinges on a meeting between João Campos and Lulu scheduled for Thursday, as Tebet and França are seen as more palatable to center and center-right voters, with potential to attract the second Senate vote.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1: ministro do Trabalho diz esperar aprovação de PEC no Senado no 1º semestre
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho hopes the Senate will approve in the first semester the PEC reducing the workweek to 40 hours and ending the 6x1 schedule, following its swift passage in the Chamber of Deputies. He noted the Senate's sensitivity to the issue, driven by women and youth, and said 30 days would suffice for voting if prioritized. President Lula praised the Chamber's approval as an 'extraordinary conquest of Brazilian society'.

item.title: Lula defendeu votar escala 4x3 ao considerar que PL estava blefando em proposta
item.description: President Lula stated he would support the 4x3 work scale proposal, advocated by the PL, while the Chamber of Deputies voted to end the 6x1 scale. He considered the PL to be bluffing in its proposal and decided to back the vote in favor of the more flexible alternative. The remark was made to ministers and allies during Wednesday’s plenary session (27).

item.title: Volta dos EUA de Flávio tem tietagem no aeroporto e reedição de grito por ‘mito’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) returned to Brazil after meeting with Donald Trump in the U.S. and was greeted by supporters at Brasília airport, who chanted 'mito, mito' as in the 2018 campaign. He did not speak to the press and remains silent on the R$134 million loan request from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the 'Dark Horse' film.

item.title: Aliados tentam repetir estratégia de Bolsonaro e mobilizam apoiadores para recepcionar Flávio em aeroporto
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro mobilized supporters to greet him at the airport following his meeting with Donald Trump, aiming to replicate the mobilization strategy used by Jair Bolsonaro in past campaigns. The effort took place on Thursday afternoon (May 28, 2026) to boost the visibility of the PL-RJ presidential pre-candidate. The initiative reflects an attempt to capitalize on his perceived closeness with international leaders and strengthen his electoral base.

item.title: Foto com três radicais é o inverso da moderação pretendida por Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attempted to position himself as a moderate, but a photo alongside Donald Trump, his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, and the grandson of the last military dictator undermines this image, revealing contradictions in his electoral strategy. The publication suggests he is aligning with radical figures, conflicting with the sensible discourse he sought to project. The event occurred on May 28, 2026 and was widely reported in the media.

item.title: Conselho de Comunicação Social debate na segunda desinformação nas eleições
item.description: The Social Communication Council of Congress will debate on Monday (1st) the risks of disinformation and artificial intelligence use in the 2026 elections, with a hearing at 9:30 AM and a deliberative meeting in the afternoon. The event, proposed by councilor Angela Cignachi, will feature experts from the TSE, academia, and civil society, and will be interactive via the Senate’s Ombudsman phone line or the e‑Citizenship Portal.

item.title: Nova pesquisa indica desgaste de Flavio
item.description: A new poll shows political wear on Flávio Dino, with Lula maintaining an advantage outside the margin of error, though still in a technical tie. His relationship with Vorcaro and the undisclosed loan undermine his image as a serious politician, especially after the Federal Police reopened the plea bargain, which may reveal further damaging information.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro perde gordura junto ao eleitorado conservador
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has lost significant support among conservative voters, particularly among the wealthy, those identifying with center-right politics, and young voters from the Lava Jato generation, following revelations about his ties to Daniel Vorcaro. This decline reflects a weakening of his traditionally solid anti-PT base in high-income, liberal-conservative niches.

item.title: Polícia do Senado pede apuração de plano de atentado de Deolane contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Senate Legislative Police filed an occurrence report to investigate statements by funk artist MC Misa, who accused influencer Deolane Bezerra of plotting an attack against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a 2026 presidential candidate. The claims were made in an interview on the Frank Clips TikTok and YouTube channel, with the video attached to the report. Police are requesting a preliminary verification of the information’s credibility, noting the statements are the interviewee’s responsibility.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Improbidade administrativa e Justiça gratuita – sessão de 28/5/2026
item.description: The STF is reviewing several actions challenging the Administrative Improbity Law, including provisions requiring intent (dolo) for wrongdoing, reducing penalties and prescription periods. Also on the agenda are ADIs filed by CSPM, Conamp, and PSB, plus RE 656558 on whether a mayor’s dispensing of bidding for legal hiring constitutes improbity, and ADC 80 assessing whether self-declaration of poverty suffices for free justice in labor courts post-2017 labor reform.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não registrou missão oficial com ônus para viagem aos EUA, diz Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro traveled to the U.S. from May 24–28 without filing an official mission request with Senate expenses, as required only when costs are covered by the Chamber. He met with Donald Trump, J.D. Vance, and Marco Rubio, stating the meetings aimed to advocate for labeling PCC and CV as terrorist groups and to showcase international backing for his presidential bid. The Lula government viewed the trip as an effort to divert attention from the Banco Master scandal, tied to alleged money requests from financier Daniel Vorcaro for the 'Dark Horse' film.

item.title: União entre Caiado e Zema esbarra no ‘radicalismo’ do Novo e na ‘neutralidade’ do PSD
item.description: A potential alliance between Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) for the 2026 elections faces significant obstacles despite the potential to sum voter intentions and oppose Lula. Key challenges include determining the head of the ticket, as both are technically tied in polls (3%-5%), and ideological conflicts: Novo seeks to maintain its identity as antipetist right-wing and survive programmatically, while PSD aims to grow without definitively aligning with either PT or PL, making the alliance unnatural given their contradictory strategies.

item.title: O que acontece se Trump declarar PCC e CV terroristas, como quer Flávio Bolsonaro?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro urged Donald Trump to designate the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, which could enable the U.S. to deploy legal, financial, and diplomatic tools to pressure Brazil. Experts warn that even the mere possibility of such a move could create instability and weaken Lula’s government. While Trump has applied similar logic to Mexican cartels, scholars note that PCC and CV are profit-driven criminal gangs, not ideologically motivated terrorist groups.

item.title: Petrobras anuncia reajuste nos preços da gasolina após subsídio
item.description: Petrobras announced a R$0.48 per liter increase in gasoline A for distributors starting May 29, 2026, accompanied by a R$0.44 per liter government subsidy, resulting in a net increase of R$0.04 per liter (1.5%). For consumers, the impact will be R$0.03 per liter on gasoline C sold at pumps.

item.title: La reforma que permite anular elecciones por “injerencia extranjera” avanza en el Congreso entre alertas de la oposición
item.description: Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies approved a constitutional reform allowing election annulments in cases of proven foreign interference, with 307 votes in favor, 128 against, and one abstention. The ruling coalition defends the change as a shield against external threats, while the opposition warns it lacks thorough analysis and could be applied arbitrarily. The reform now awaits Senate approval in the coming hours.

item.title: Lula realiza 4ª aplicação de radioterapia preventiva
item.description: President Lula underwent his fourth session of preventive superficial radiotherapy at Sírio-Libanês Hospital in Brasília following the removal of a basal cell carcinoma from his scalp in April. The treatment protocol consists of 15 applications over three weeks, administered Monday through Friday according to his presidential schedule, with each session lasting approximately two minutes. Lula resumes normal duties at the Palácio do Planalto after each procedure.

item.title: Lula vende terreno na Lua para o trabalhador
item.description: The text criticizes the approval of the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale in the Chamber of Deputies, arguing that despite claims of improving workers' lives, the measure will likely worsen their conditions. The author claims the PEC's authors lack solid foundations and that the proposal serves interests contrary to those of workers. The title 'Lula sells lunar land to the worker' is used ironically to highlight the falseness of the promise.

item.title: Alcolumbre acelera PEC da oposição e impõe risco à tramitação do fim da 6×1 no Senado
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre accelerated the processing of an alternative PEC to the proposal ending the 6×1 work schedule, sending it directly to the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) just hours after it was filed by the opposition. The initiative, led by Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), proposes a work-hour-based hiring model and expands direct negotiation between employers and employees, reacting to the Chamber-approved PEC that reduces the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours. The move comes amid a dispute over the pace of the main PEC’s review, with Alcolumbre avoiding commitment to an accelerated process, despite not indicating intent to block it.
